name: Albuquerque
tagline: High Desert Beauty, Ancient Culture, and Balloon-Filled Skies
description: Albuquerque sits at the crossroads of Native American and Hispanic heritage in a stunning high-desert landscape at the foot of the Sandia Mountains. The cost of living is remarkably low for a metro of nearly one million, sunshine is abundant with over 310 days per year, and the cultural richness is unmatched. From the International Balloon Fiesta to Old Town's centuries-old adobe architecture, Albuquerque offers FIRE retirees a deeply affordable and uniquely beautiful place to call home.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe in most residential areas; higher property crime in some neighborhoods
quickFacts.climate: Semi-arid with mild winters, hot summers, low humidity, and over 310 sunny days per year

housing.description: Modest studio or older 1BR in a workable outer area (West Mesa, University-adjacent, safe Southeast blocks)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with Hatch chile; casual New Mexican meals out occasionally

healthcare.description: A subsidized ACA marketplace Silver plan, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600 for a single person; New Mexico added its own state subsidy for 2026 to soften that cutoff. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance (transit is minimal; a car is near-mandatory)

entertainment.description: Hiking the Sandia foothills, Old Town wandering, the public library; an occasional film night

1M.lifestyle: A modest studio or older one-bedroom in a workable outer neighborhood, with home cooking the norm and Hatch chile in everything. Healthcare and the near-mandatory car form a hard cost floor even here, but Albuquerque's best assets — hiking the Sandia foothills, wandering Old Town, and 310 days of sun — cost nothing. The ACA Silver premium stays low only if MAGI is managed under the 2026 ~$62,600 subsidy cliff, and New Mexico's unique state backfill softens the math. A frugal but genuinely livable high-desert base.

housing.description: Decent 1BR in a solid neighborhood — Nob Hill or the Northeast Heights

dining.description: Regular casual dining along Central Avenue and in Old Town; local craft breweries

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost stays low if MAGI is managed under the cliff (NM's state backfill helps)

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage for mountain and pueblo day trips

entertainment.description: Sandia Peak Tramway passes, Balloon Fiesta tickets, KiMo Theatre shows, a gym membership

2M.lifestyle: A decent place in Nob Hill or the Northeast Heights, dining out several times a week along Central Avenue and among the craft breweries, and a reliable car for trips to pueblos and national monuments. A Sandia Peak Tramway pass and Balloon Fiesta tickets fit easily. Coverage is comfortable and the overall cost base leaves real breathing room at Albuquerque prices.

housing.description: Quality 1BR or small adobe in a desirable area — Nob Hill or the North Valley

dining.description: Frequent quality dining at spots like Campo and Los Poblanos; wine events

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan; the line is padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits phase out

transportation.description: A late-model SUV for desert and mountain excursions, premium insurance

entertainment.description: Hot-air-balloon rides, Santa Fe Opera trips, a golf membership, Canyon Road art

3M.lifestyle: A quality one-bedroom or small adobe in Nob Hill or the North Valley, frequent dinners at Campo and Los Poblanos, and a late-model SUV for desert and mountain excursions. A golf membership, hot-air-balloon rides, and trips to the Santa Fe Opera and Canyon Road galleries all fit the budget. Healthcare is a padded Gold plan near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff. An affluent, low-friction life with substantial margin at local prices.

housing.description: Upscale condo or small custom home rental in Sandia Heights or the North Valley

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the best tables in ABQ and Santa Fe; occasional private-chef meals

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized Gold/Platinum plan plus concierge / direct primary care

transportation.description: A luxury SUV plus a second vehicle; occasional flights from ABQ

entertainment.description: Private balloon flights, Santa Fe Opera patronage, art collecting, a country club membership

domesticHelp.description: Weekly deep cleaning plus xeriscape and property maintenance

luxuryExtras.description: Regular art purchases, quarterly travel, Balloon Fiesta VIP experiences

5M.lifestyle: A custom adobe in Sandia Heights or a North Valley property with acreage, weekly housekeeping, and concierge-level care on an unsubsidized premium plan. Near-daily fine dining across Albuquerque and Santa Fe, a country club membership, and business-class flights are routine. Private balloon flights, Santa Fe Opera patronage, and regular Canyon Road art purchases round out the calendar.

housing.description: Top-of-market luxury home or estate rental in Sandia Heights or the luxury North Valley

dining.description: Private-chef dining and the finest farm-sourced tables across the region

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized plan plus concierge medicine — fully out of subsidy range

transportation.description: A premium SUV with full ownership costs, plus regular private car service

entertainment.description: Major arts patronage, private gallery events, international travel, exclusive cultural experiences

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping several days a week plus xeriscape and grounds service

luxuryExtras.description: First-class travel, a major art collection, cultural philanthropy, a Santa Fe pied-à-terre

10M.lifestyle: A grand Sandia Heights home or a North Valley hacienda, with housekeeping and grounds help several days a week and occasional private-chef evenings alongside the region's best tables. First-class travel, top-tier concierge medicine, and daily fine dining are unremarkable at this level, and a Santa Fe pied-à-terre is within reach. Albuquerque's low cost base makes this genuinely lavish living — roughly $184k a year — with large monthly margins.
